Subject: Pinecrest Systems — private deployment network runbook & on-prem package kickoff

Hi Sofia / Laura,

Thanks again for the platform demo last week. Pinecrest is ready to proceed with a private deployment and we want to get the networking and on-prem packaging logistics aligned before the vendor kickoff next Wednesday. Our priorities are: VPC peering, private endpoints for the ingestion API, and the on-prem appliance packaging checklist (airgap-friendly).

Quick background:
- Environment: prod and staging in us-west-2 (AWS)
- Primary contact for networking: it-ops@pinecrest.com (copied below)
- Target cutover window: 2027-07-20 to 2027-07-22 (flexible by one week)

Questions we want to resolve in this thread:
1) IP ranges and egress controls required for the on-prem package to reach Redwood control plane (we need CIDR allowlists).
2) DNS and private endpoint naming conventions for the ingestion and metrics endpoints.
3) Packaging format for airgapped sites (tarball + install manifest vs container OCI image).
4) A single-run runbook draft we can hand to our SREs and integrator.

Attached is our current network inventory (internal VLANs, firewall model). Please confirm which pieces you need from us and any pre-flight checks Redwood requires. Also looping in Ryan (external consultant) who will help on our side for the appliance install.

Thanks — Eva

[Attachment: pinecrest_network_inventory.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

--
Eva Nguyen
Head of Platform Engineering | Pinecrest Systems
eva@pinecrest.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pinecrest Systems — private deployment network runbook & on-prem package kickoff

Hi Eva — welcome and thanks for the inventory. Laura and I reviewed the spreadsheet and put together an initial runbook draft and a packaging recommendation for airgapped installs. I attached the runbook draft (PDF) and the Redwood on-prem package v1.2 tarball (installer + manifest).

High-level answers and next steps:
- CIDR/egress: Redwood control plane accepts outbound to the following CIDRs over HTTPS (443): 52.23.17.0/24, 34.198.64.0/20, 3.237.120.0/22. For the streaming control channel we prefer a persistent outbound TLS connection; if you restrict by FQDN, the control endpoints are: control-runner.redwood.ai and events.redwood.ai.
- Private endpoints: we recommend dedicated private DNS names per environment: api.internal.pinecrest.redwood and metrics.internal.pinecrest.redwood. We'll provide a private endpoint manifest for AWS PrivateLink/Interface Endpoint.
- On-prem packaging: for airgap we recommend tarball + signed manifest (not OCI) because Pinecrest stated they have limited registry access. The attached tarball includes an install.sh and a signed manifest.json; installation flow documented in runbook-draft-20270615.pdf.

Immediate asks from Redwood:
1) Confirm whether pinecrest runs a NAT gateway for your on-prem site (if yes, provide outbound IPs).
2) Confirm the DNS zone owner for private records (so we can share an exact records file).
3) Let us know a good 60-min slot tomorrow for a joint networking review with your SREs (Laura + Marcus will join from our side).

Proposed slot: Wed 2027-06-16 09:00-10:00 PT. If that works we'll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Attachments: runbook-draft-20270615.pdf; redwood_onprem_package_v1.2.tar.gz

Thanks,
Sofia

Sofia Ivanova

Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pinecrest Systems — private deployment network runbook & on-prem package kickoff

Thanks Eva / Sofia — quick technical notes from our side (copying the relevant runbook section inline):

1) Firewall rules: allow outbound TLS to the three CIDRs Sofia listed; on the appliance allow inbound from your internal management VLAN only (we include a sample iptables/ufw snippet in the runbook).

2) MTU and dual-stack: Pinecrest should verify MTU is >= 1400 for encrypted tunnels; we recommend dual-stack where possible but the control channel works on IPv4-only.

3) Secrets and KMS: for private deployments we support either customer-managed KMS (recommended) or Redwood-hosted keys. If you choose customer-managed KMS, we'll need the ARN and a short test token exchange during the install window (documented in section 4).

4) PrivateLink specifics: we will provide an AWS CloudFormation snippet to create the VPC endpoint service and the interface endpoint consumer — please confirm which AWS account ID we should target for that template.

I captured these as comments in the runbook PDF. Marcus and I will be on the call tomorrow.

Laura

--
Laura Bennett
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
